assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
a fixed downstream consumer with an enumerable decision/field set exists; 'lossless' is defined relative to that field set, not literal bit-losslessness
the consumer's tokenizer is known and used to measure token cost
the source is available in full at generation time so faithfulness can be checked by entailment against it
exclusions: human-readability and stylistic quality of the brief (the target is machine parsing)
literal bit-level lossless compression (provably infeasible below the source entropy floor at a tight budget)
training or fine-tuning the downstream consumer model
general open-domain abstractive summarization quality metrics decoupled from a downstream field set
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for decision-lossless rate-distortion summarization work units, grounded in Shannon's rate-distortion and source coding theory, Rissanen's MDL, and faithfulness research in abstractive summarization; no supplied dataset
source_citation: Shannon 1948 A Mathematical Theory of Communication (source coding theorem and rate-distortion); Cover & Thomas 2006 Elements of Information Theory (ch. 10 rate-distortion theory, ch. 5 data compression); Rissanen 1978 Modeling by Shortest Data Description (Minimum Description Length); Maynez, Narayan, Bohnet & McDonald 2020 On Faithfulness and Factuality in Abstractive Summarization (ACL)

competency_questions.question: What is the fixed downstream field set and what content must be preserved for it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIELD_SET_SPEC fixes the field set; MUST_PRESERVE_CLASSES maps content to it

competency_questions.question: Why can a brief not be both literally lossless and arbitrarily short, and what is the rate floor?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOURCE_ENTROPY_BOUND sets the entropy floor; RATE_DISTORTION frames the tradeoff

competency_questions.question: How is source content partitioned into must-preserve versus droppable, and in what order is it shed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MUST_PRESERVE_CLASSES and DROPPABLE_CLASSES partition; SALIENCE_RANKING orders shedding

competency_questions.question: How is distortion defined so that 'lossless' means the right thing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISTORTION_METRIC defines distortion as decision error over the field set, not surface overlap

competency_questions.question: How is the lossless-versus-efficient goal reframed as a rate-distortion tradeoff and an operating point?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RATE_DISTORTION reframes it (FP2); OPERATING_POINT and DECISION_LOSSLESS pick the target

competency_questions.question: What does decision-losslessness mean and how is it operationally tested?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DECISION_LOSSLESS defines it; ROUND_TRIP_TEST tests it operationally

competency_questions.question: How is the operating point and token budget chosen given per-field loss tolerance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OPERATING_POINT selects the point; TOKEN_BUDGET fixes and measures B

competency_questions.question: How is the token budget measured and how does distortion vary with it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOKEN_BUDGET measures cost; DISTORTION_CURVE traces distortion vs budget

competency_questions.question: How is the operating budget validated against coverage and the distortion knee?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISTORTION_CURVE locates the knee; COVERAGE_AUDIT validates coverage and budget jointly

competency_questions.question: Why is the brief optimized for machines and what target does that set?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MACHINE_FACING sets the parse-optimized target; DENSE_GRAMMAR realizes it

competency_questions.question: What grammar makes the dense line self-describing and unambiguously parseable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DENSE_GRAMMAR fixes the pipe/KV format; SCHEMA_HINT and ABBREVIATION_KEY make it self-describing

competency_questions.question: Which compression operators move along the rate axis and how is their distortion controlled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPRESSION_OPS applies lossless/bounded-lossy operators ordered by SALIENCE_RANKING

competency_questions.question: How is faithfulness enforced and how is each fact made verifiable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FAITHFULNESS forbids hallucination; VERIFIABILITY_TAGS attach provenance

competency_questions.question: How is decision-losslessness verified end-to-end before the brief is accepted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUND_TRIP_TEST reconstructs decisions; VERIFIABILITY_TAGS support the audit

glossary.definition: R(D): the minimum rate (bits/tokens) needed to encode a source within distortion D; the lower boundary of the achievable (rate,distortion) region
lossless with respect to a fixed downstream field set: the consumer makes every field decision identically from the brief and from the source
the field-restricted entropy of the source; a lower bound on the rate of any zero-distortion code by Shannon's source coding theorem
decision error over the field set: weighted fraction of downstream field decisions the brief would get wrong versus the source
the chosen (token budget, tolerated distortion) pair on R(D) that the brief targets
a content class load-bearing for at least one downstream field, whose loss can flip a decision (identifiers, quantities, negation, deadlines)
a content class that is redundant, inferable, or decision-irrelevant and may be compressed or removed
a compact self-description prepended to the dense line declaring field names, order, types, and a version so the line is self-parsing
content in the brief not entailed by the source: extrinsic (absent from source) or intrinsic (contradicting source), per Maynez et al. 2020
feeding the brief alone to the downstream consumer and checking it reconstructs every field decision correctly; the operational test of decision-losslessness
Rissanen's MDL principle: prefer the model+data encoding of shortest total length; here, splitting cost between a shared codebook and the message

nodes.definition: Fix the exact set of fields/decisions a downstream consumer (a generator, classifier, or router) must make from the brief alone; this field set is the reference against which 'lossless' is defined and is the boundary condition for the whole rate-distortion problem.

base.update_signal: downstream consumer's required field set or decision contract changes

pros.claim: Pinning the field set turns 'lossless' from an unbounded ideal into a finite, checkable obligation per field
pros.example: fields={priority, owner, due_date, blocking_dep} -> only these four must be reconstructable

cons.claim: A field set fixed too early can omit a decision the consumer silently needs, making the brief locally lossless but globally wrong
cons.example: consumer later needs 'risk_tier' that was never enumerated

failure_modes: unenumerated decision relied on downstream
field set conflated with source schema rather than decision needs
acceptance_tests: every downstream decision maps to at least one enumerated field with a criticality weight
revisit_triggers: a new decision field is requested

nodes.definition: Estimate the information content of the source restricted to the field set, establishing the rate floor: by Shannon's source coding theorem no lossless code can compress decision-relevant content below its entropy, so 'lossless AND arbitrarily short' is provably impossible.

base.update_signal: source distribution assumptions or field-restricted entropy estimate changes

pros.claim: An explicit entropy floor exposes the hard limit: tokens cannot go below the field-restricted entropy without distortion
pros.example: if the four decision fields carry ~30 bits, no zero-distortion brief is shorter than ~30 bits of code

cons.claim: Entropy of natural-language fields is hard to estimate; a wrong floor mis-prices the achievable budget
cons.example: treating a high-entropy free-text justification as if it were a low-entropy enum

failure_modes: entropy underestimated -> impossible budget targeted
source modeled as i.i.d. when it has strong dependencies
acceptance_tests: the chosen token budget is consistent with (>=) the estimated field-restricted entropy floor

nodes.definition: Partition source content into classes that MUST survive compression because they are load-bearing for at least one downstream field: identifiers, quantities, polarity/negation, deadlines, named entities, and explicit constraints whose loss flips a decision.

base.update_signal: field set changes or a content class is reclassified as decision-relevant

pros.claim: Naming must-preserve classes makes preservation a typed, auditable obligation rather than an editorial hope
pros.example: negation and numeric quantities are tagged must-preserve so 'not approved' never compresses to 'approved'

cons.claim: Over-broad must-preserve sets defeat compression by protecting content no decision actually needs
cons.example: marking every proper noun must-preserve when only the assignee entity is decision-relevant

failure_modes: a decision-flipping token (a negation, a unit) dropped as droppable
must-preserve set so large no budget is feasible
acceptance_tests: every must-preserve class traces to >=1 downstream field and survives the round-trip test
revisit_triggers: a dropped token is found to have flipped a decision

nodes.definition: Identify content classes that are redundant, inferable, or decision-irrelevant and therefore compressible or droppable: rhetorical framing, repeated restatements, hedging, examples that re-encode an already-stated fact, and stylistic prose.

base.update_signal: droppable taxonomy or redundancy model changes

pros.claim: Explicitly classing content as droppable is where almost all rate savings come from; redundancy is free to remove
pros.example: three paragraphs restating one due date collapse to a single date token

cons.claim: Aggressive dropping can remove content that is redundant in the source but disambiguating for the consumer
cons.example: an 'example' that is the only place a unit is stated gets dropped as illustrative

failure_modes: inferable-but-not-actually-recoverable content dropped
redundancy mis-detected across negation boundary
acceptance_tests: dropped content is provably reconstructable or provably decision-irrelevant under the field set
revisit_triggers: a 'droppable' drop degrades a downstream decision

nodes.definition: Define the distortion measure d(source, brief) as decision error over the field set -- the fraction or weighted count of downstream fields the consumer would get wrong from the brief versus from the source -- NOT token edit distance or surface n-gram overlap.

base.update_signal: distortion definition or field weighting changes

pros.claim: A decision-indexed distortion makes 'lossless' precise: zero distortion = the consumer makes every field decision identically from the brief
pros.example: distortion counts a flipped 'blocking=true->false' as full loss regardless of token overlap

cons.claim: Decision-error distortion needs a downstream oracle or proxy to evaluate, which can be expensive or noisy
cons.example: approximating consumer decisions with an LLM judge introduces its own error

failure_modes: distortion proxied by surface overlap, rewarding faithful-looking but decision-wrong briefs
field weights mis-set so a critical flip scores low
acceptance_tests: distortion is computed from downstream field decisions, not surface overlap, and weights sum to a fixed total
revisit_triggers: distortion metric found to reward decision-wrong output

nodes.definition: Frame the core tension: the achievable region of (rate=tokens, distortion=decision error) pairs is governed by a rate-distortion function R(D); lower distortion costs more rate. 'Lossless AND minimal tokens' is not a point but a tradeoff bounded by R(0)>=source entropy on the field set.

base.update_signal: rate-distortion model or achievable-region assumptions change

included: FP2 reframing of lossless+efficient as a tradeoff

pros.claim: Casting the problem as R(D) dissolves the contradiction in 'lossless AND token-efficient': they trade off along a curve, and the right question is which point to pick
pros.example: at D=0 rate equals the entropy floor; relaxing to D=0.02 may halve the tokens

cons.claim: The true R(D) for natural-language field reconstruction is not closed-form; we work with an empirically traced approximation
cons.example: the curve is sampled at a few budgets, not derived analytically

failure_modes: treating zero distortion as free (ignoring R(0) floor)
assuming a single 'best' point exists independent of the consumer's loss tolerance
acceptance_tests: the stated goal is expressed as a point on a rate-distortion tradeoff, never as simultaneous literal-lossless + minimal-token
revisit_triggers: achievable region re-traced and shifts materially

nodes.definition: Define decision-losslessness: the brief is lossless w.r.t. a fixed downstream field set iff the consumer makes every field decision identically from the brief and from the full source (distortion=0 under the decision metric). This is strictly weaker than literal/bit-losslessness and is the property actually required.

base.update_signal: definition of the downstream field set or the losslessness criterion changes

pros.claim: Decision-losslessness is achievable at far lower rate than literal losslessness because it only protects what changes a decision
pros.example: a 50-page contract compresses to a few decision fields while remaining decision-lossless for an approval router

cons.claim: Decision-losslessness is only as trustworthy as the field set; it is silent about decisions outside that set
cons.example: a brief decision-lossless for routing is useless to an auditor who needs the dropped clauses

failure_modes: claiming losslessness without naming the field set
field set narrower than the consumer's actual decisions
acceptance_tests: for every field, the consumer's decision from the brief equals its decision from the full source on a held-out test set
revisit_triggers: a consumer decision diverges between brief and source

nodes.definition: Choose the operating point on R(D): the (token budget, tolerated distortion) pair to target, given the consumer's loss tolerance per field. Decision-critical fields demand the D=0 point; advisory fields may tolerate small distortion to buy rate.

base.update_signal: consumer loss tolerance or budget constraint changes

pros.claim: Selecting the point explicitly makes the lossless/efficient tradeoff a deliberate, documented decision rather than an accident of prompt length
pros.example: set D=0 for {amount, party, deadline}; allow D<=0.05 for {tone, background}

cons.claim: A single global operating point can over- or under-protect heterogeneous fields with different stakes
cons.example: one budget forces the same fidelity on a legal amount and a stylistic note

failure_modes: operating point chosen without per-field tolerance
point set below the entropy floor (infeasible at zero distortion)
acceptance_tests: the selected operating point is feasible (rate>=entropy floor at the chosen distortion) and per-field tolerances are recorded

nodes.definition: Fix a token budget B for the brief and measure realized token cost against it with a concrete tokenizer; the budget is the rate axis made operational, and cost must be measured in the same tokenizer the downstream consumer uses.

base.update_signal: tokenizer or budget constraint B changes

pros.claim: A measured budget in the consumer's own tokenizer makes 'token-efficient' an enforced number, not an aspiration
pros.example: B=180 tokens measured with the same BPE the downstream model parses with

cons.claim: Budgets measured in the wrong tokenizer mislead: a brief 'within budget' in one tokenizer overflows another
cons.example: counting whitespace-split words while the consumer uses sub-word BPE

failure_modes: cost measured in a different tokenizer than the consumer's
budget set without reference to the entropy floor
acceptance_tests: realized token cost <= B measured with the consumer's tokenizer, and B >= the entropy floor

nodes.definition: Trace the empirical distortion-vs-budget curve by generating briefs at several budgets and measuring decision distortion at each, approximating R(D) and locating the knee where further compression starts flipping decisions.

base.update_signal: curve sampling protocol or distortion measurement changes

pros.claim: An empirical curve replaces guesswork: it shows exactly how many tokens buy how much fidelity for THIS source and field set
pros.example: curve shows distortion is flat from 250 down to 180 tokens, then rises sharply -> pick ~180

cons.claim: The curve is only valid for the sampled source/consumer; it does not generalize to a different document or field set
cons.example: a curve traced on invoices misapplied to legal briefs

failure_modes: curve sampled too coarsely to locate the knee
distortion measured with a proxy that hides decision flips
acceptance_tests: the curve has enough budget samples to locate the knee, and the chosen budget sits at or above it
revisit_triggers: source or field set changes (curve invalidated)
curve knee moves materially on re-sampling

nodes.definition: Commit to optimizing the brief for machine parsing rather than human readability: prose connectives, hewing to natural prosody, and narrative flow are dropped in favor of token-dense, position-stable, unambiguously parseable structure.

base.update_signal: downstream consumer changes from machine to human or vice versa

pros.claim: Optimizing for the parser removes whole classes of tokens (articles, transitions, hedges) that cost rate but carry no decision information
pros.example: 'The owner of the task is, as noted, Alice' -> 'owner=Alice'

cons.claim: Machine-facing briefs are hostile to human review, so errors are harder for a person to spot before consumption
cons.example: a flipped boolean in a pipe-delimited line is invisible at a glance

failure_modes: machine-facing form so terse it becomes ambiguous to the parser
human reviewer assumed where only a parser consumes
acceptance_tests: the brief parses unambiguously under the declared grammar with no reliance on prose connectives
revisit_triggers: consumer switches to a human reader
parser ambiguity observed on the brief form

nodes.definition: Fix a dense, self-describing grammar -- a stable pipe/key-value line format with a leading schema_hint -- so the brief is unambiguously parseable and self-delimiting; the grammar is part of the code, paid for once, and amortized across every field.

base.update_signal: grammar specification or delimiter set changes

pros.claim: A fixed grammar with a schema_hint lets the dense line self-describe, so the consumer parses it deterministically without a separate spec
pros.example: '#schema:owner|prio|due|blocks; owner=Alice|prio=P1|due=2026-07-01|blocks=SVC-9'

cons.claim: A rigid grammar can fail to encode an unexpected field shape, forcing either an escape hatch or silent loss
cons.example: a multi-valued field that the single-value KV slot cannot hold

failure_modes: delimiter collision with field content (unescaped pipe in a value)
grammar drift between producer and consumer versions
acceptance_tests: the brief carries a schema_hint and every field parses unambiguously; delimiters in values are escaped
revisit_triggers: a parse failure traced to the grammar

nodes.definition: Prepend a compact schema_hint that names the fields and their order/types so the dense line is self-describing; this is the one-time grammar cost that makes the rest of the line interpretable and version-checkable by the consumer.

base.update_signal: field set or schema versioning policy changes

pros.claim: A schema_hint makes the brief portable and version-checkable: the consumer validates the field set before parsing values
pros.example: '#v=2;fields=owner:str,prio:enum,due:date' lets the consumer reject a v1 parser

cons.claim: The schema_hint is pure overhead at very small budgets where its tokens rival the payload
cons.example: a 4-field hint costs as much as the 4 values it describes

failure_modes: schema_hint omitted, leaving the consumer to guess field order
schema version not bumped on a field change
acceptance_tests: the schema_hint declares every field and a version tag, and the consumer validates it before parsing

nodes.definition: Maintain an expandable abbreviation/symbol key so high-frequency long tokens are coded to short symbols recoverable by the consumer; this is an MDL move -- shifting cost into a shared, amortized codebook to lower the message rate.

base.update_signal: abbreviation codebook or sharing assumption changes

pros.claim: By MDL, moving repeated long strings into a shared key lowers total description length when the codebook is amortized over many briefs
pros.example: code 'organization'->'org', 'requirement'->'req' once, save tokens on every line

cons.claim: If the consumer lacks the key (or it drifts), abbreviations are unrecoverable and the brief becomes lossy
cons.example: a brief using an org-specific code shipped to a consumer without the codebook

failure_modes: abbreviation collides with a literal value
codebook drift between producer and consumer
acceptance_tests: every abbreviation in the brief is expandable by the consumer's current key with no collisions
revisit_triggers: an unexpandable abbreviation reaches the consumer

nodes.definition: Enforce faithfulness: every fact in the brief must be entailed by the source -- no hallucinated, fabricated, or unsupported content. Following Maynez et al. 2020, distinguish extrinsic hallucination (content not in source) from intrinsic (content contradicting source); both are zero-tolerance for decision fields.

base.update_signal: faithfulness definition or entailment-checking method changes

pros.claim: Faithfulness keeps compression honest: a shorter brief is worthless if it invents a deadline or flips a polarity
pros.example: abstractive rewrite that introduces a date absent from the source is rejected as extrinsic hallucination

cons.claim: Strict entailment can reject valid sound inferences the consumer would accept, forcing verbose hedging
cons.example: an obvious aggregate the source implies but does not literally state is flagged unsupported

failure_modes: abstractive paraphrase silently introduces an unsupported fact
intrinsic hallucination flips a polarity (approved<->denied)
acceptance_tests: every decision-field value in the brief is entailed by the source on a faithfulness check
revisit_triggers: a hallucinated fact is found in a shipped brief

nodes.definition: Attach verifiability tags (source span pointer, or an explicit 'inferred'/'derived' marker) to facts in the brief so the consumer can distinguish source-grounded values from derived ones and audit any field back to the source.

base.update_signal: provenance tagging scheme or source addressing changes

pros.claim: Verifiability tags let the consumer trust-but-verify and let an auditor trace any decision back to a source span cheaply
pros.example: owner=Alice[span:p2L4] vs risk=high[inferred] makes provenance explicit

cons.claim: Provenance tags add rate; at tight budgets they compete with the payload they describe
cons.example: a span pointer per field can double the token cost of a terse brief

failure_modes: inferred value presented as if source-grounded
span pointers stale after source revision
acceptance_tests: every fact carries a provenance tag (source span or inferred marker) that resolves against the current source
revisit_triggers: a span pointer fails to resolve

nodes.definition: Run the round-trip test: hand the brief alone (no source) to the downstream consumer and check whether it reconstructs every field decision correctly. This is the operational definition of decision-losslessness and the primary acceptance gate.

base.update_signal: round-trip protocol or consumer model changes

pros.claim: The round-trip test directly measures the property that matters: can the consumer act correctly from the brief alone
pros.example: feed only the dense line to the router; confirm it picks the same owner/priority as from the full ticket

cons.claim: The test is only as representative as the consumer model and the held-out cases used to run it
cons.example: passing on easy cases while failing on the rare decision-flipping edge case not in the sample

failure_modes: round-trip run with the source still in context (leakage)
test cases miss the decision-critical edge cases
acceptance_tests: the consumer reconstructs every field decision from the brief alone, matching the source-based decision on the test set
revisit_triggers: a round-trip failure is observed in production

nodes.definition: Rank source content units by decision salience -- expected reduction in downstream decision error if retained -- so that under a binding budget the highest-salience must-preserve content is encoded first and droppable content is shed last.

base.update_signal: salience model or field weighting changes

pros.claim: Ranking by decision salience makes budget cuts principled: you lose the least decision-relevant content first
pros.example: a binding constraint clause outranks a background paragraph for retention

cons.claim: Salience estimates are noisy; a mis-ranked but decision-critical unit can be shed under a tight budget
cons.example: an easily-overlooked exception clause scored low and dropped

failure_modes: salience proxied by frequency, demoting rare-but-critical clauses
ranking ignores field weights from the operating point
acceptance_tests: retained content is ordered by decision salience and no must-preserve unit is shed before any droppable unit
revisit_triggers: a high-salience unit is found to have been shed

nodes.definition: Apply the compression operators that move along the rate axis: lossless ones (deduplication, abbreviation, normalization to canonical form) and bounded-lossy ones (paraphrase, aggregation, quantization of low-stakes fields), each tagged by the distortion it may introduce.

base.update_signal: compression operator set or per-operator distortion budget changes

pros.claim: Separating lossless from bounded-lossy operators lets you spend the distortion budget deliberately and only where the operating point allows
pros.example: normalize dates losslessly; quantize a 'confidence 0.73' to 'high' only for advisory fields

cons.claim: Composed lossy operators accumulate distortion that can exceed the per-field tolerance non-obviously
cons.example: paraphrase plus aggregation together flip a decision neither would alone

failure_modes: lossy operator applied to a D=0 decision field
accumulated distortion across operators exceeds the field tolerance
acceptance_tests: each operator's distortion is accounted, and the summed distortion per field stays within its tolerance from the operating point
revisit_triggers: accumulated distortion exceeds a field tolerance

nodes.definition: Audit the final brief on both axes at once: field-set coverage (every required field is present and decision-lossless via the round-trip) and budget conformance (cost <= B). A pass requires both; either failure routes back to operating-point or compression.

base.update_signal: audit criteria or budget/coverage thresholds change

pros.claim: A joint audit prevents optimizing one axis at the other's expense: it fails a brief that is cheap but decision-lossy or lossless but over budget
pros.example: 180-token brief that drops 'blocking_dep' fails coverage even though it meets budget

cons.claim: Joint pass/fail can stall when no point satisfies both (entropy floor exceeds budget), needing escalation not iteration
cons.example: budget below the field-restricted entropy floor makes a clean pass impossible

failure_modes: coverage passed but a decision field silently absent
budget conformance measured in the wrong tokenizer
acceptance_tests: the brief is decision-lossless over the full field set AND within budget B, both measured with the consumer's tokenizer

nodes.definition: Define when a previously-passing brief must be regenerated: the field set changes, the source is revised, the consumer/tokenizer changes, or a production round-trip failure is observed. Each trigger invalidates a specific upstream artifact, scoping the rework.

base.update_signal: trigger taxonomy or invalidation mapping changes

pros.claim: Mapping each trigger to the specific invalidated artifact scopes rework: a tokenizer change re-measures budget without re-deriving the field set
pros.example: source revision invalidates entropy floor and curve but not the field set spec

cons.claim: Over-eager triggers cause needless regeneration; under-eager ones let a stale brief drift into decision loss
cons.example: regenerating on a cosmetic source edit that touches no decision field

failure_modes: a decision-relevant source change does not trigger revision
trigger fires but invalidates the wrong artifact, missing the real staleness
acceptance_tests: every trigger maps to the precise upstream artifact it invalidates and scoped regeneration restores a passing audit
revisit_triggers: a stale brief reaches production without a trigger firing

edges.why_related: the traced distortion curve feeds back to relocate the operating point at the knee
a round-trip failure feeds back to back off a lossy compression operator
a failed audit routes back to reselect the operating point or budget
a field-set-change trigger reopens the field set specification
the entropy floor constrains feasible operating points to rate>=floor at zero distortion
per-field distortion tolerances from the operating point bound which lossy operators may apply
provenance tags let the round-trip audit attribute a decision flip to a specific source span
the schema_hint enumerates the fields the coverage audit checks for presence

edges.resolution_rule: respect the entropy floor: hold decision-losslessness for D=0 fields and spend rate to meet it; only relax distortion on fields whose operating-point tolerance allows, never compress a D=0 field below its floor
edges.why_related: driving the token budget down conflicts with decision-losslessness once the budget approaches the entropy floor
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the rate-distortion outcome

edges.resolution_rule: terseness must not introduce ambiguity that the consumer resolves into an unsupported fact; keep every dense token entailed by the source and add a verifiability tag rather than guess
edges.why_related: maximal machine-facing terseness can drop qualifiers, risking an unfaithful over-strong claim
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the rate-distortion outcome

edges.resolution_rule: apply lossy operators only to fields whose operating-point distortion tolerance is non-zero; route any operator that would flip a D=0 field's decision back to a lossless alternative
edges.why_related: aggressive lossy compression to hit the budget conflicts with keeping decision-critical fields lossless
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the rate-distortion outcome

edges.resolution_rule: only abbreviate with symbols the consumer's current codebook expands; if the consumer cannot expand a symbol, prefer the longer literal even though it costs rate
edges.why_related: abbreviation saves rate but, if the codebook is not shared, makes the brief unparseable by the machine consumer
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the rate-distortion outcome

conflict_axes.name: decision_lossless_vs_token_budget
conflict_axes.description: Driving tokens down toward the entropy floor eventually starts flipping decisions; holding decisions exact costs rate. This is the central FP2 rate-distortion tension.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pick an operating point on R(D); hold D=0 only for decision-critical fields, never compress them below the floor

conflict_axes.name: literal_lossless_vs_decision_lossless
conflict_axes.description: Literal/bit-losslessness is bounded below by source entropy and usually infeasible at a tight budget; decision-losslessness only protects what changes a decision.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: adopt decision-losslessness over a named field set; document that out-of-set content is intentionally not preserved

conflict_axes.name: machine_facing_vs_human_readable
conflict_axes.description: Parse-optimized density removes prose overhead but makes human review and error-spotting hard.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: optimize for the parser; gate with an automated round-trip rather than human readability

conflict_axes.name: faithfulness_vs_compression
conflict_axes.description: Aggressive abstractive compression risks extrinsic/intrinsic hallucination; strict entailment limits how far you can compress.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: permit only entailment-preserving operators on decision fields; tag inferred values explicitly

conflict_axes.name: must_preserve_breadth_vs_budget
conflict_axes.description: A broad must-preserve set protects more content but defeats the budget; a narrow one risks dropping a decision-flipping token.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: include in must-preserve only content tracing to a field; rank the rest by decision salience

conflict_axes.name: abbreviation_savings_vs_recoverability
conflict_axes.description: Codebook abbreviation lowers message rate (MDL) but is unrecoverable if the consumer lacks or drifts from the key.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: abbreviate only with a shared, version-checked codebook; fall back to literals otherwise

conflict_axes.name: provenance_completeness_vs_rate
conflict_axes.description: Per-fact verifiability tags enable audit but cost tokens that compete with the payload at tight budgets.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tag decision-critical and inferred fields; omit tags for self-evident source-grounded enums

conflict_axes.name: empirical_curve_cost_vs_point_accuracy
conflict_axes.description: Sampling more budgets locates the knee precisely but costs many generations; coarse sampling is cheap but mis-places the operating point.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sample densely only near the suspected knee; coarse elsewhere

conflict_axes.name: early_field_set_freeze_vs_late_discovery
conflict_axes.description: Freezing the field set early enables all downstream work but risks omitting a decision the consumer later needs; deferring it stalls everything.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: freeze the field set against the consumer's decision contract; treat additions as a revision trigger

edge_cases.description: The field-restricted entropy floor exceeds the imposed token budget, so no decision-lossless brief fits the budget.
edge_cases.trigger: budget B set below the source entropy floor on the must-preserve fields
edge_cases.mitigation: escalate: raise B, narrow the field set, or accept bounded distortion on non-critical fields; do not silently drop a decision field

edge_cases.description: A negation or unit is compressed away, flipping a decision while the brief still looks faithful and fluent.
edge_cases.trigger: a must-preserve token (negation, quantity, unit) classed as droppable
edge_cases.mitigation: tag negation/quantity/identifier as must-preserve; round-trip test detects the decision flip

edge_cases.description: Abstractive paraphrase introduces a fact absent from the source (extrinsic hallucination) that the consumer treats as real.
edge_cases.trigger: lossy paraphrase applied without an entailment check
edge_cases.mitigation: gate every value with source entailment; mark derived values 'inferred'

edge_cases.description: The brief is decision-lossless for the named field set but the consumer silently needs a field never enumerated.
edge_cases.trigger: field set fixed without the full decision contract
edge_cases.mitigation: validate the field set against the consumer's decision contract; treat a new decision as a revision trigger

edge_cases.description: Token cost is measured in a different tokenizer than the consumer uses, so a 'within budget' brief overflows downstream.
edge_cases.trigger: cost measured with a word-split or wrong-BPE tokenizer
edge_cases.mitigation: always measure cost in the consumer's tokenizer

edge_cases.description: An abbreviation symbol is unrecoverable because the consumer's codebook drifted or was never shared.
edge_cases.trigger: abbreviation used outside a shared, version-checked codebook
edge_cases.mitigation: version the codebook and validate it before parsing; fall back to literals on mismatch

edge_cases.description: A pipe or delimiter appears unescaped inside a field value, corrupting the parse and shifting subsequent fields.
edge_cases.trigger: delimiter collision with field content in the dense grammar
edge_cases.mitigation: escape delimiters in values; the schema_hint lets the consumer detect field-count mismatch

edge_cases.description: The distortion curve is sampled too coarsely and the operating point is placed past the knee, in the region where decisions flip.
edge_cases.trigger: budget sweep with too few samples near the knee
edge_cases.mitigation: densify sampling near the knee; choose a budget at or above it

edge_cases.description: Composed lossy operators each within tolerance accumulate to flip a field neither would alone.
edge_cases.trigger: paraphrase plus aggregation applied to the same field without summed-distortion accounting
edge_cases.mitigation: account summed per-field distortion across operators; stop before the field tolerance is exceeded

edge_cases.description: A source revision changes a decision-relevant value but the cached brief is reused without regeneration.
edge_cases.trigger: source updated with no revision trigger fired
edge_cases.mitigation: fire a source-revision trigger that invalidates the entropy floor, curve, and brief; re-audit

edge_cases.description: The round-trip test passes because the source leaked into the consumer's context, masking a decision-lossy brief.
edge_cases.trigger: round-trip run with the full source still in context
edge_cases.mitigation: run the consumer on the brief alone with the source removed from context

edge_cases.description: Distortion is scored by surface n-gram overlap, rewarding a faithful-looking brief that nonetheless flips a decision.
edge_cases.trigger: distortion proxied by ROUGE-style overlap instead of decision error
edge_cases.mitigation: score distortion by downstream decision error, not surface similarity

workflow.description: Enumerate the downstream consumer's required fields/decisions and assign criticality weights; this is the losslessness reference.
workflow.gate: every downstream decision maps to >=1 weighted field

workflow.description: Estimate the field-restricted source entropy to set the rate floor and compressibility headroom.
workflow.gate: floor estimated; budget will be checked against it

workflow.description: Partition content into must-preserve (decision-relevant) and droppable (redundant/inferable) classes.
workflow.gate: every must-preserve class traces to a field

workflow.description: Define distortion as weighted decision error over the field set, not surface overlap.
workflow.gate: distortion computed from field decisions with fixed weights

workflow.description: Express the lossless-and-efficient goal as a point on R(D); confirm zero-distortion rate >= entropy floor (FP2).
workflow.gate: goal stated as an operating point, not literal-lossless+minimal

workflow.description: Choose the (budget, per-field distortion tolerance) point; D=0 for decision-critical fields.
workflow.gate: point feasible (rate>=floor) with recorded per-field tolerances

workflow.description: Fix budget B and measure realized cost in the consumer's tokenizer.
workflow.gate: cost <= B in the consumer's tokenizer; B >= floor

workflow.description: Fix the pipe/KV grammar with a schema_hint and abbreviation key; encode the dense, machine-facing line.
workflow.gate: line parses unambiguously with a schema_hint and escaped delimiters

workflow.description: Apply salience-ordered lossless then bounded-lossy operators to meet B, accounting per-field distortion.
workflow.gate: summed per-field distortion within tolerance; no lossy op on a D=0 field

workflow.description: Check every value is source-entailed; attach verifiability tags and mark inferred values.
workflow.gate: no extrinsic/intrinsic hallucination on decision fields

workflow.description: Feed the brief alone to the consumer and compare its field decisions against source-based decisions.
workflow.gate: consumer reconstructs every field decision from the brief alone

workflow.description: Audit coverage and budget jointly; on pass, register revision triggers; on fail, route back.
workflow.gate: decision-lossless over the field set AND within budget B

dominance_rules.rule: FIELD_SET_SPEC must be fixed before MUST_PRESERVE_CLASSES, DISTORTION_METRIC, or any budget work
dominance_rules.rationale: the field set is the reference for losslessness; classifying or measuring distortion first causes rework
dominance_rules.trigger: content classification or distortion definition begins without a fixed field set
dominance_rules.action: block until the field set is fixed against the decision contract

dominance_rules.rule: The token budget must never be set below the field-restricted entropy floor for zero-distortion fields
dominance_rules.rationale: by Shannon's source coding theorem a sub-floor budget cannot be decision-lossless on those fields
dominance_rules.trigger: a budget below the entropy floor is proposed for D=0 fields
dominance_rules.action: raise the budget, narrow the field set, or relax distortion on non-critical fields; never compress a D=0 field below floor

dominance_rules.rule: Distortion must be measured as decision error over the field set, not surface overlap, wherever the two disagree
dominance_rules.rationale: surface metrics reward faithful-looking but decision-wrong briefs
dominance_rules.trigger: a surface-overlap distortion proxy is used for acceptance
dominance_rules.action: replace the proxy with a decision-error measure via the round-trip test

dominance_rules.rule: No lossy compression operator may be applied to a field whose operating-point distortion tolerance is zero
dominance_rules.rationale: a lossy op on a D=0 field can flip a decision and break decision-losslessness
dominance_rules.trigger: a lossy operator targets a decision-critical field
dominance_rules.action: substitute a lossless operator or back off the operator

dominance_rules.rule: FAITHFULNESS gating must pass before ROUND_TRIP_TEST is trusted
dominance_rules.rationale: a hallucinated value can pass a round-trip that the consumer cannot distinguish from truth
dominance_rules.trigger: round-trip run on a brief with unverified entailment
dominance_rules.action: run the entailment check and tag provenance before the round-trip

dominance_rules.rule: ROUND_TRIP_TEST must be run on the brief alone, with the source removed from context
dominance_rules.rationale: source leakage masks a decision-lossy brief
dominance_rules.trigger: round-trip executed with the source still in context
dominance_rules.action: strip the source from context and re-run on the brief alone

dominance_rules.rule: Abbreviations may only be used when the consumer's current, version-checked codebook expands them
dominance_rules.rationale: an unexpandable abbreviation makes the brief lossy and unparseable
dominance_rules.trigger: an abbreviation is emitted without a shared codebook entry
dominance_rules.action: expand to the literal or add the symbol to the shared codebook first

dominance_rules.rule: COVERAGE_AUDIT must pass on both axes (decision-lossless AND within budget) before acceptance
dominance_rules.rationale: optimizing one axis at the other's expense yields a cheap-but-lossy or lossless-but-overbudget brief
dominance_rules.trigger: a brief passes only one of coverage or budget
dominance_rules.action: route back to operating-point or compression; never accept a single-axis pass

dominance_rules.rule: A revision trigger must fire whenever the field set, source, or consumer/tokenizer changes
dominance_rules.rationale: a stale brief silently drifts into decision loss
dominance_rules.trigger: a decision-relevant change occurs with no trigger
dominance_rules.action: fire the trigger, invalidate the mapped upstream artifact, and re-audit

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not classify content or define distortion before the field set is fixed; a late field set invalidates both
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-classifying content and re-deriving distortion after the field set changes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not target a budget below the entropy floor; discovering infeasibility after encoding wastes the whole pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: encoding and compressing toward an impossible zero-distortion budget

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not use surface-overlap distortion as the acceptance metric; swapping it in late re-opens every operating-point decision
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-tracing the distortion curve after the metric is corrected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not apply lossy operators to decision-critical fields; reverting a decision-flip found at audit means regenerating
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating the brief after a lossy op flips a D=0 field

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not measure budget in the wrong tokenizer; an overflow found downstream forces a re-encode
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-encoding after a 'within budget' brief overflows the consumer's tokenizer

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not abbreviate without a shared, version-checked codebook; an unexpandable symbol forces a re-encode at the consumer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-encoding after the consumer cannot expand an abbreviation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not run the round-trip with the source in context; a false pass surfaces as a production decision failure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shipping a decision-lossy brief that passed a leaked round-trip

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not omit revision triggers; an undetected source/field/tokenizer change surfaces as silent drift requiring full reanalysis
anti_rework_rules.prevents: full re-derivation after a stale brief drifts undetected into decision loss

iteration_protocol.trigger: the entropy floor exceeds the token budget (no feasible zero-distortion brief)
iteration_protocol.action: escalate via OPERATING_POINT: raise B, narrow FIELD_SET_SPEC, or relax distortion on non-critical fields

iteration_protocol.trigger: the round-trip test shows a decision flip from the brief alone
iteration_protocol.action: trace the flipped field to its compression operator and back off, re-checking faithfulness

iteration_protocol.trigger: a hallucinated (extrinsic/intrinsic) fact is found on a decision field
iteration_protocol.action: tighten FAITHFULNESS entailment and add verifiability tags, then re-run the round-trip

iteration_protocol.trigger: the coverage audit fails on the budget axis while coverage passes
iteration_protocol.action: re-locate the operating point at the distortion-curve knee and re-apply salience-ordered compression

iteration_protocol.trigger: a must-preserve token was found shed under a tight budget
iteration_protocol.action: re-rank by decision salience and protect the token as must-preserve before re-compressing

iteration_protocol.trigger: the consumer's tokenizer or codebook changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-measure budget in the new tokenizer and re-validate the abbreviation key before re-auditing
fire a revision trigger that reopens FIELD_SET_SPEC and invalidates the dependent must-preserve, distortion, and curve artifacts

priority_rationale: FIELD_SET_SPEC and SOURCE_ENTROPY_BOUND are foundational; DISTORTION_METRIC, RATE_DISTORTION and DECISION_LOSSLESS encode the FP2 reframing; OPERATING_POINT/TOKEN_BUDGET fix the rate; grammar and compression realize the brief; faithfulness, round-trip, and the joint coverage audit close decision-losslessness last.
